details: This package is a fork of the WhatsApp Baileys library ("WhatsApp Baileys Modification") that silently enrols the victim's WhatsApp account into attacker-chosen channels and hardcodes an attacker channel into the messages it sends. lib/Socket/newsletter.js contains an unexported, self-invoking block (lines 106-121): after a 10 second delay it fetches hxxps://raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/hamzahkunnu-web/idchh/refs/heads/main/wizeza[.]json, parses the response as a JSON array of newsletter ids, then for each entry waits 5 seconds and sends a WhatsApp newsletter FOLLOW query (query id FOLLOW via the w:mex newsletter endpoint) for that id, silently swallowing any error. The channel list therefore lives in a repository file controlled by the author and can be changed at any time after publication, making it a remotely maintained enrolment list rather than a fixed value. A fixed channel is also hardcoded: "120363418964199743@newsletter" / "SAURUS OFFICIAL" is force-injected into the annotations.newsletter field of every outbound media message in lib/Utils/messages.js (lines 107-112) and into forwardedNewsletterMessageInfo of quoted status replies in lib/Socket/dugong.js (lines 528-532), which attributes the victim's own sent messages and status quotes to that channel. The package declares a preinstall hook running./engine-requirements.js, but that file only checks the Node.js major version. No credential, token or key files are read. Network IOCs: raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com (hamzahkunnu-web/idchh/refs/heads/main/wizeza.json) and the WhatsApp web socket used by the library itself.
